claim: The logical Cartesian plane. For parity laws C1, C2 and their product law (allowed states: arrays whose columns are allowed states of C1 and whose rows are allowed states of C2): (1) if K1 is a knot of C1 through p, p' and K2 a knot of C2 through q, q', the L-shaped set (K1 x {q'}) xor ({p} x K2) is a knot of the product of |K1| + |K2| - 2 places through (p,q) and (p',q'), so bond distance <= delta1 + delta2 - 1; (2) the product of two two-way threads on Z^2 has dense finite moves generated by one move of diameter 1, so it splits at range 1 (LOGIC-AXIS A) and its bond distance lies between the sup and the taxicab distance up to constants, with bond balls of radius r holding Theta(r^2) distinctions: a plane of dimension two built from two logical number lines. (3) Not proved, a conjecture with finite evidence: bond distance = delta1 + delta2 - 1 exactly (855 pairs of two thread products, no exception).
